content:
Earlier in July this year, Apple added a basic search feature update to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed by users, but the same TestFlight app update introduced an extremely annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't noticeably affected by this bug. So at the time I felt the TestFlight update was a simple but important step.

Sometimes a small change can have a major impact. For users with a large pile of pre-loaded software on hand, Apple's latest TestFlight update illustrates this point perfectly. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds "a search field to quickly find relevant apps".

Looking back, I did notice some odd things, which I mentioned at the end of the article (but my judgment was exactly the opposite):

I think the reason I didn't notice this was the so-called bug is because two years ago I "merged" multiple TestFlight apps I had used for years into my iCloud and App Store Apple account. Although the process was very tedious, it was worth it for me.

In any case, the TestFlight bug did not escape the keen eyes of John Vorhees from MacStories:

So, you can imagine how excited I was when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac saying that TestFlight finally had a search field added. "Finally," I thought to myself. I immediately stopped what I was doing to update that app. [...] Unfortunately, there is a big "however" to this. In the past, TestFlight betas were arranged in reverse chronological order, and I personally really liked this arrangement. [...] Well, now those expired betas are scattered among the active betas arranged in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I have ever participated in. I did a rough count, and for me there are nearly 800 app entries. As you can imagine, the active betas among them are very few. The search function is helpful, but it's no longer possible to scroll through to find things.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally rolled out an update for TestFlight. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update did indeed fix the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is the fix for this regression.
